answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent's reputation to a scarce, verifiable stake rather than to free accounts: an agent that wants to trade must lock collateral and build a history of fulfilled work, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. Like saffron, genuine reputation is expensive to grow and easy to spot as fake; a sybil standing on the ledge of a new identity has no track record, and peers can demand an opal-clear proof of past performance before trusting it with anything valuable.
